features.name: arg_self_meta_platform_or_status
features.definition: Does the OP's argument contain explicit self-referential meta-commentary about platform mechanics or the author's own status?
features.spec: Read only the `argument` text (OP's argument body; not title). Return 1 if the OP's own text explicitly comments on itself/their own posting in terms of platform mechanics (e.g., subreddit rules, delta system/mechanics, moderation, posting/formatting/edit features, votes/karma, how the post was submitted) or on the author's own status (e.g., being new/long-time user, account status, credentials, who they are as poster). Return 0 if no such commentary. Exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates (e.g., 'EDIT: view changed, delta awarded') and reports of the outcome; these do not count as evidence. Generic discussion of platform rules not about the OP's own post/status is not self-referential. Quoted text from others does not count unless the OP adopts it. If argument is missing or malformed return null; empty string returns 0.

h0: Discussions with and without self-referential meta-commentary in the argument (arg_self_meta_platform_or_status) have the same probability of view change.
h1: Discussions with arg_self_meta_platform_or_status=1 have a lower probability of view change than those with 0.
note: Operational assumption: presence (binary) of meta-commentary on platform mechanics or author status, using the OP argument only. Current argument text may include edits and outcome announcements added after the discussion; these are excluded by the semantic rule, but timing of the text relative to outcome is unknown. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only.
